## Multiple Choice Questions

**1.** For the Charles River invoice lines of fiscal 2026, the average line total is about half again as large as the median line total. What does this suggest about the distribution of line totals?

A.  It is symmetric, so the average and the median describe the typical line equally well.
B.  It is skewed to the left, with a minority of very small lines pulling the average down.
C.  It is skewed to the right, with a minority of large lines pulling the average up.
D.  It contains errors, because the average and the median of accounting data should be equal.

**2.** What is the difference between STDEV.S and STDEV.P?

A.  STDEV.S treats the values as a sample and divides by their number minus one, while STDEV.P treats them as the whole population and divides by their number.
B.  STDEV.S ignores blank cells, while STDEV.P counts them as zeros.
C.  STDEV.S returns the spread around the median, while STDEV.P returns the spread around the mean.
D.  STDEV.S works only on Excel Tables, while STDEV.P works on any range.

**3.** An analyst wants the median line total of fiscal 2026 invoice lines only. Why does the formula `=MEDIAN(FILTER(InvoiceLines[LineTotal],InvoiceLines[FiscalYear]=2026))` use FILTER?

A.  FILTER sorts the values, which MEDIAN requires.
B.  FILTER converts the line totals from text to numbers.
C.  FILTER removes the outliers that would distort the median.
D.  MEDIAN accepts no criteria and Excel has no MEDIANIFS, so FILTER supplies only the rows that meet the condition.

**4.** A summary uses `=SUMIFS(InvoiceLines[LineTotal],InvoiceLines[ItemGroup],"Furnture")`, with the group name misspelled. What does the formula return?

A.  The error #N/A, because no row matches the criterion
B.  Zero, without an error, which a comparison with a control total would reveal
C.  The total of every row, because an invalid criterion is ignored
D.  The Furniture total, because SUMIFS corrects near matches

**5.** In Tutorial 6.1, the revenue of the four product lines falls short of the fiscal 2026 control total by exactly the revenue of the Services item group. What does the difference show?

A.  The control total double-counts some invoice lines.
B.  The SUMIFS formulas of the product lines contain an error.
C.  The summary leaves out a category that is part of the population, and it is complete only when the category is added.
D.  Services revenue should be excluded from the control total.

**6.** A text field, such as CustomerSegment, is dragged into the Values area of a PivotTable. How does Excel summarize it by default?

A.  It counts the rows.
B.  It sums the values.
C.  It lists each value.
D.  It returns an error, because text cannot be summarized.

**7.** An analyst defines a PivotTable calculated field with the formula `=Quantity*UnitPrice` to show revenue. What does the field return for each cell of the PivotTable?

A.  The revenue of the cell, because the formula is applied to each row and the results are summed
B.  The sum of the quantities multiplied by the sum of the unit prices, which is not the revenue
C.  The average revenue per line in the cell
D.  An error, because calculated fields cannot multiply two fields

**8.** A PivotTable shows fiscal 2026 revenue with item groups in its rows and quarters in its columns. What does Show Values As % of Column Total display?

A.  Each quarter's share of the item group's revenue for the year
B.  Each value's share of the revenue of all groups and quarters together
C.  The change in each group's revenue from the previous quarter
D.  Each item group's share of the quarter's revenue

**9.** A formula on the Bridge worksheet refers to the PivotTable with `=GETPIVOTDATA("Sum of Quantity",Drivers!$A$3,"Period","2026-Q3")` rather than with a cell address such as `=Drivers!B5`. What is the advantage?

A.  GETPIVOTDATA identifies the value by its field and item, so it keeps returning the right value when the PivotTable's layout changes.
B.  GETPIVOTDATA refreshes the PivotTable whenever the formula recalculates.
C.  GETPIVOTDATA reads the value from the source Table, so the PivotTable can be deleted.
D.  GETPIVOTDATA rounds the value to the number format of the PivotTable.

**10.** An analyst adds a custom column to the InvoiceLines query and loads the query, but the new field does not appear in a PivotTable built from InvoiceLines. What is the most likely explanation?

A.  PivotTables cannot use columns added by Power Query.
B.  The custom column must first be converted to values.
C.  A PivotTable summarizes its own copy of the data, which updates only when the PivotTable is refreshed, for example with Refresh All.
D.  The PivotTable must be deleted and built again.

**11.** A PivotTable of the Charles River general ledger shows negative revenue for the Furniture account in the fourth quarter of fiscal 2026. What is the most likely cause?

A.  Credit memos issued in the fourth quarter exceeded the invoices.
B.  The year-end closing entry, which debits every revenue account on the last day of the year, is included in the PivotTable.
C.  The PivotTable sums debits and credits in the wrong columns.
D.  The Furniture Seasonal Promotion reduced revenue below zero.

**12.** In a margin bridge, what does the mix effect measure?

A.  The change in margin caused by selling more or fewer units in total
B.  The change in margin caused by charging different prices for the same items
C.  The change in margin caused by a change in the standard cost of each item
D.  The change in margin caused by a shift in sales between items that earn different margins

**13.** Why is the cost effect zero in the Furniture margin bridge of Tutorial 6.3?

A.  The Furniture product line has no cost of goods sold.
B.  Costs are excluded from the bridge because they are recorded in the ledger.
C.  InvoiceLines values every quantity at the item's standard cost, and each item has a single standard cost, so the cost of the same items cannot differ between the quarters.
D.  The cost effect is combined with the volume effect in every bridge.

**14.** From the third quarter to the fourth, the Furniture margin at standard cost falls, while the margin before promotional discounts rises slightly. What can you conclude?

A.  The decline comes from the promotional discounts, not from list prices, the items sold, or their costs.
B.  The decline comes from higher standard costs in the fourth quarter.
C.  The decline comes from a fall in the number of units sold.
D.  The two margins are calculated inconsistently, so no conclusion is possible.

**15.** Under the PCAOB's standard on substantive analytical procedures, what should an auditor do before evaluating the difference between recorded revenue and an expectation?

A.  Ask management for the expected amount and accept it if it is close to the recorded amount.
B.  Develop the expectation from plausible relationships and decide how large a difference can be accepted without further investigation.
C.  Replace the expectation with the recorded amount of the previous year.
D.  Select a random sample of transactions, because analytical procedures cannot use expectations.
